# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-flash-flash_10-low-comm-combined

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Tests all three communication interventions together (**Message Delivery Timing**, **Message Board / Threading**, and **Message Intent Tags**) on `gemini-3-flash-preview` (`low` thinking, 100 steps, compaction at 28K, per-turn step counter) across `flash_10`. Urgent `Request` and `Proposal` messages deliver immediately while `FYI`, `ACK`, and `Response` messages wait up to 4 steps for a clean workflow boundary; `FYI` messages do not open unresolved threads; `--intent ACK --reply-to <id>` resolves threads automatically; and open `Request`/`Proposal` threads persist across 28K context compactions. Compared directly against `coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-flash-flash_10-low-stepcounter` (6/10 overall, 3/10 clean-merge passes).

## Observations

- Clean-merge pass rate rose from 3/10 (30%) on the baseline to 4/10 (40%): `openai_tiktoken_task/0` merged cleanly and `typst_task/6554` reconciled into identical branches (both were merge conflicts rescued only by single-branch fallback in the baseline), alongside clean passes on `go_chi_task/26` and `huggingface_datasets_task/6252`.
- Combining intent routing with threading and boundary-timed delivery cut total message chatter by 45% (from 167 messages in baseline to 92, or 9.2 per pair) at comparable cost (`$4.10` vs. `$4.24`), opening 16 non-`FYI` coordination threads and resolving 13 (81%) with zero command-parse or API retry errors.
- Combining all three rescued the `2/10` pass-rate drop seen under standalone threading (`coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-flash-flash_10-low-threading`), showing that excluding `FYI` status chatter from opening threads and pairing threads with boundary-timed delivery prevents premature verbal closure.
